# LeakSanitizer suppressions for the loft interpreter ASan leak gate (@PLN85).
# Syntax: `leak:<substr>` suppresses any leak whose stack contains a frame whose
# symbolized name contains <substr>.
#
# CROSS-SYMBOLIZER RULE: the two CI legs symbolize differently, so every entry
# below is a BARE function/type name chosen to be a substring of BOTH forms:
#   - Linux uses llvm-symbolizer  → DEMANGLED Rust: `loft::fill::append_text`.
#   - macOS uses the system `atos` → MANGLED   Rust: `..._4loft4fill11append_text`
#     (llvm-symbolizer is NOT forced on macOS: it leaves the dyld system frames
#     unsymbolized, so the thread-TLS class below could never match — atos resolves
#     them). A bare leaf/module name (`append_text`, `ir_read`) is a substring of
#     both the mangled (length-prefixed `11append_text`) and demangled forms, so
#     one file works on both legs. NEVER write a `module::fn` form here — the `::`
#     is absent from the mangled name and the macOS leg would leak through.
#
# The interpreter interns IR node/schema/store names (and reconstructed string
# content) as `&'static str` via an intentional, bounded `Box::leak` (interner-style,
# not a growing leak) when loading IR back from a store. The SAME class lives in three
# sibling modules — the allocating frame names the module, so each needs its own line:
# `ir_read::{read_db_content,read_block,read_definition}`,
# `ir_schema::{block_from_parsed,definition_from_parsed}`, and
# `database::snapshot::content_from` (matched by the bare `snapshot`). ~16
# ir_read/ir_schema/store round-trip lib tests report it. Documented in miri.yml.
# Every real interpreter leak stays visible and is gated by the shrinking count
# baseline (scripts/asan_leak_ratchet.sh).
leak:ir_read
leak:ir_schema
leak:snapshot

# The SAME interner class on the PARSE side (loft#876): a field's declared TEXT default
# (`label: text = "hi"`) folds to a `Content::Str`, which is a raw `{ptr, len}` with no
# owning variant, so its spelling is interned by the same intentional `Box::leak`.
# BOUNDED by the source: one allocation per field that declares a text default, decided
# once at type registration — never one per read, and nothing here grows with runtime.
# `typedef::fold_declared_default` carries `#[inline(never)]` FOR this line: inlined, the
# allocating frame reads as `typedef::fill_database`, and suppressing that name would
# blind the gate to every allocation in the whole type-registration path.  Keep the two
# in step — dropping the attribute silently stops this suppression from matching, and the
# benign leak reds the gate again.
leak:fold_declared_default

# The SAME interner class on the DIAGNOSTIC-CACHE side (loft#1240 nightly).  A warm bundle
# load decodes cached diagnostics back into `DiagEntry`s, and the diagnostic CODE is a frozen
# public surface (DIAGNOSTICS.md), so `DiagEntry::decode_from_cache` interns each one as a
# `&'static str` through the same intentional `Box::leak` — BOUNDED by the number of distinct
# codes, deduplicated by the pool, never one per read.
#
# Reachability is why it is intermittent rather than constant: the leaked `&'static str` is
# held by a `OnceLock` pool, so Linux LSan (reachability-based) usually walks to it from the
# statics and says nothing, while a run that does not reach it reports a Direct leak.  A gate
# that depends on whether a scan happens to find a root is not a gate, so it is suppressed
# outright, like every other interner above.
#
# `decode_from_cache` is the anchor rather than `intern` or `unesc`: suppressions match by
# SUBSTRING, and `intern` is a substring of `internal` / `internally` / `internal_copies`
# (12 identifiers in src/) while `unesc` is one of `unescape_text` / `unescaped_content` (6).
# `decode_from_cache` is unique in the tree, and it encloses BOTH the `unesc` allocation and
# the `intern` call, so it survives either being inlined.  It carries `#[inline(never)]` FOR
# this line — keep the two in step, as with `fold_declared_default` above.
leak:decode_from_cache

# The fault-path text class (@PLN102).  When a loft program raises a fault (a failed
# `assert`, `panic`, a `raise`d OOB/DivByZero) WHILE a text is mid-construction, the
# compiler-emitted drop of that in-flight text local never runs, so its `String` buffer
# is live at exit.  This is an ACCEPTED non-cleanup on the terminating abort path, NOT a
# production leak: the real binary `process::exit`s on a fault, so LSan never runs there;
# it only surfaces in-process (the dozens of `should_panic` / `.error()` fixtures and the
# `raise(...)` scripts).  Freeing in-flight text on the abort path would need the
# coroutine-style zeroing/double-drop discipline on the hot call path — a risky change out
# of proportion to a non-production leak.  The four text-construction entry points
# (bare names — `fill::append_text` etc. mangle to `...11append_text` on the macOS leg):
#
# ⚠ These lines hide MORE than the fault path, and the premise that they did not was
# measured false (loft#1338): a non-faulting program that returned text from an early
# `return` or a view of a local orphaned one `String` per call through the SAME frames,
# and this gate said nothing — 14 corpus scripts leaked with no fault in them.  The
# residue that followed (loft#1357: a lambda's `??` return, a nullable text local, a
# generic's loop-variable return and its nested forwarder, a par loop's text discard, a
# tail reading its own buffer, a `??` temp consumed by a scalar or an `if` condition, a
# `parallel` arm's formatted argument) is closed too — 11 corpus scripts to 0 under the
# release sweep.  What this gate still cannot see is the CLASS: `scripts/valgrind-sweep.sh`
# (RELEASE.md § Memory safety) and `LOFT_TEXT_TIMELINE=1` are the instruments for it, and
# `tests/text_buffer_ledger.rs` holds the line.
leak:append_text
leak:format_text
leak:format_long
leak:text_tl_fmt

# The registry HTTP layer's fetch buffer / one-time client state (@PLN112 nightly).  The
# `loft install` / registry-index fetch (`registry_index::http_get_bytes`) sets up a
# process-lifetime HTTP/TLS client whose state is still REACHABLE at exit — so Linux LSan
# (reachability-based) never flags it, while macOS ASan's at-exit check does. A one-time
# client alloc, not a growing leak; any fixture that resolves a registry package surfaces
# it. macOS-only, so this line is a no-op on the Linux leg. (The three docs pages that used
# to be the ones doing it — 14-image / 21-random / 32-time — moved into their libraries in
# @PLN149 step 9; the suppression is about the HTTP layer, not about them.)
leak:http_get_bytes

# macOS `Network.framework` one-time DNS/network context (@PLN112 nightly, confirmed from the
# CI runner's raw ASan stack). The FIRST `getaddrinfo` on macOS (reached via `ureq` →
# `std::net::lookup_host` during a registry fetch) triggers Apple's NAT64 synthesis, which
# `dispatch_once`-allocates a `nw_context` hash table (`nw_context_activate` →
# `nw_hash_table_create_internal`) inside `Network.framework`. It is a process-lifetime
# singleton, reachable at exit → Linux's reachability LSan never flags it, and `getaddrinfo`
# on Linux doesn't use Network.framework at all, so this is a macOS-only no-op there. Not a
# loft (or even a ureq) heap leak — Apple's, not ours to free. The 336-byte leak on the 3
# network-doing docs fixtures whose deeper `http_get_bytes` frame sits beyond ASan's context
# limit (so the http_get_bytes line above can't reach it); `nw_context` is the in-range,
# reliably-atos-symbolized anchor.
leak:nw_context

# macOS dyld thread-local storage on a spawned thread (the test harness watchdog + `par`
# workers): `dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::addTermFunc` (term-func registration, direct) AND
# `dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::instantiateVariable` via `_tlv_get_addr` (the TLS block
# itself, indirect). BOTH are allocated INSIDE libdyld.dylib and torn down by dyld AFTER
# LSan's at-exit scan — a known LeakSanitizer-on-macOS false positive, not a loft heap
# leak, and there is no loft-side allocation to free. Matching the enclosing dyld type
# `ThreadLocalVariables` covers both frames in one line (atos resolves it; the earlier
# `addTermFunc`-only line missed the 6984-byte indirect `instantiateVariable`). Absent on
# the Linux leg (different TLS impl), so this line is a macOS-only no-op there.
leak:ThreadLocalVariables

# macOS TLS trust settings: the first certificate verification reads the system's trust
# settings through `Security.framework`, which builds its keychain singletons
# (`ModuleNexus<KeychainCore::Globals>`, the MDS directory, an autorelease-pool page, CF
# thread-specific tables) on a libdispatch worker thread inside `dispatch_once` — so no loft
# or HTTP frame is on the stack and `http_get_bytes` above cannot reach them.  Process-
# lifetime state Apple never frees, reachable at exit; Linux verifies with no such framework,
# so this line is a macOS-only no-op there.  First seen on lib/audience_crystal's
# 01-editor-helpers.loft (nightly run 37767550180, 14 of its 15 allocations).
leak:__SecTrustSettingsCopyCertificates

# macOS CoreAnalytics' at-exit barrier: `CoreAnalytics::Client::sendExitBarrierWithTimeoutSync`
# `dispatch_async`s one 64-byte block from Apple's own `atExitHandler`, after which nothing
# runs to free it.  Allocated during exit by the OS, not by loft (the 15th allocation above).
leak:sendExitBarrierWithTimeoutSync
